question: The phenomenon in which different parts of the plant, like root, stem and leaves, develop into new plants under appropriate conditions is called _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vegetative propagation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** in plants where new individual plants are produced from the **vegetative parts** of the parent plant, such as **roots, stems, or leaves**.
 
• In this process, the offspring produced are **genetically identical** to the parent plant, essentially acting as **clones**. This ensures that desirable characteristics of the parent are preserved in the next generation.
 
• Unlike sexual reproduction, this phenomenon does not involve the **fusion of gametes** or the **production of seeds**. It allows plants to reproduce even if they have lost the ability to produce viable seeds.
 
• The process occurs under **appropriate environmental conditions** (moisture, temperature, and nutrients), where specialized structures like **buds** present on the vegetative parts develop into **adventitious roots** and shoots. ***Hence, the correct answer is Vegetative propagation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sexual Reproduction:** 
 
 
• This method involves the **fusion of male and female gametes** (pollen and ovules) to produce a **zygote**, which eventually develops into a **seed**.
 
• It results in **genetic variation** among the offspring, which is crucial for evolution and adaptation to changing environments. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fertilisation:** 
 
 
• **Fertilisation** is the specific biological process of the **union of a sperm cell with an egg cell**.
 
• In flowering plants (**Angiosperms**), this occurs within the **ovary** after **pollination**. It is a step within the cycle of sexual reproduction rather than the name of the propagation method itself. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Regeneration:** 
 
 
• **Regeneration** is the ability of an organism to **regrow lost or damaged body parts**. While some simple organisms like **Hydra** or **Planaria** can give rise to a whole new individual from a small fragment, in the context of higher plants developing from roots/stems/leaves, the term vegetative propagation is more appropriate. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Methods of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• **Natural methods** include **tubers** (Potato), **rhizomes** (Ginger), **runners** (Strawberry), and **bulbs** (Onion).
 
• **Artificial methods** are widely used in **horticulture** and include **cutting** (Rose), **grafting** (Mango), and **layering** (Jasmine).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Plants raised by this method can bear **flowers and fruits earlier** than those produced from seeds.
 
• It is the only method for reproducing plants that do not produce seeds, such as **banana, orange, rose, and jasmine**.
 
• The **uniformity** of the crop is maintained since all plants are **clones** of the parent, which is highly beneficial for **commercial farming** and **agriculture**.
 
• One notable example is the **Bryophyllum** plant, which produces **buds** in the margins of its **leaves**; if these leaves fall on moist soil, each bud can develop into a **new plantlet**.
